definitions.power: Does the other person hold authority, status, or seniority over the speaker, such that deference is owed regardless of familiarity? 0 = no authority; 1 = high authority.
definitions.distance: How socially unfamiliar or unrelated are the two people, independent of power? 0 = very close; 1 = complete stranger or institutional relationship.
definitions.context: How institutional, transactional, or high-stakes is the interaction itself, independent of who the person is? 0 = casual or personal; 1 = highly institutional or high-stakes.

formal_warm.reason: An elder relative is socially close and the interaction is low-stakes, but age and family role still require deference; threshold-only assignment would incorrectly produce Respectful Casual.

reverse_formal.reason: In a service-worker-to-customer interaction, the speaker owes deference because the power direction is inverted, so the interaction is a distinct type rather than a point on the ordinary dial.

scenarios.name: Friend
scenarios.justification: No authority, close, purely casual.

scenarios.name: Younger sibling
scenarios.justification: No authority, closest possible, no stakes.

scenarios.name: Spouse/partner
scenarios.justification: No authority, maximally close, personal.

scenarios.name: Classmate
scenarios.justification: Peer, slight unfamiliarity if not close friends, low stakes.

scenarios.name: Auto driver
scenarios.justification: No real authority, stranger, brief transaction.

scenarios.name: Shopkeeper
scenarios.justification: No authority, stranger, transactional but routine.

scenarios.name: Delivery person
scenarios.justification: No authority, stranger, brief and routine.

scenarios.name: Colleague (peer)
scenarios.justification: No hierarchy, moderately familiar, workplace context raises stakes slightly.

scenarios.name: Stranger asking directions
scenarios.justification: No authority, total stranger, but trivial low-stakes ask.

scenarios.name: Grandparent/elder relative
scenarios.justification: High deference owed by age and family role, but very close with low institutional stakes; assigned by tag because the numeric threshold would understate the required deference.

scenarios.name: Landlord
scenarios.justification: Some authority through control of housing, fairly distant, moderately transactional.

scenarios.name: Bank employee
scenarios.justification: Institutional authority, stranger, high-stakes interaction involving money.

scenarios.name: Receptionist
scenarios.justification: Mild institutional authority, stranger, moderately formal setting.

scenarios.name: Hotel/front-desk staff
scenarios.justification: Service interaction with a stranger in an institutional setting, similar to a receptionist.

scenarios.name: Boss/manager
scenarios.justification: Direct authority over the speaker combined with workplace stakes.

scenarios.name: Teacher
scenarios.justification: High authority, moderate familiarity, educational stakes.

scenarios.name: Doctor
scenarios.justification: Expert authority, social distance, and high health-related stakes.

scenarios.name: Job interviewer
scenarios.justification: High authority over the outcome, stranger, maximum stakes.

scenarios.name: Police officer
scenarios.justification: Institutional and legal authority, stranger, high-stakes interaction.

scenarios.name: Customer (you as service worker)
scenarios.justification: The speaker owes deference to the customer because the ordinary power direction is inverted; assigned by interaction-type tag rather than a dial threshold.
